newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical second-quarter profits rise 4.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical second-quarter profits rise 4.6 percent.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co. said Thursday its second-quarter earnings edged up 4.6 percent as strong volume growth and a one-time gain helped it overcome a $200 million price decline.
The second-largest U.S. chemical concern said it earned $571 million, or $2.48 a share, during the second quarter, vs. $546 million, or $2.20 a share, for the same period last year.

But excluding one-time events, Dow's earnings for the period would have been $518 million, or $2.25 a share. The events included a gain of $98 million from the sale of its stake in Destec Inc., which was partially offset by $46 million in charges from an insurance restructuring, shutdown of facilities in Texas and from its DowElanco agricultural unit.

The second-quarter, per-share results, excluding the one-time items, slightly exceeded Wall Street's consensus estimate of $2.20 as published by First Call. But Dow stock was down $1.625 at $89.06 in consolidated midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Dow's revenues for the period were $5.37 billion, up from $5.18 billion a year ago based on strong worldwide volume volume growth of about 8 percent.
The volume growth, combined with reduced operating expenses and the favourable impact of currency on costs, offset a price decline of $200 million from the second quarter of 1996.

Prices were down in all geographic locations and all core business segments compared with a year ago with the exception of the plastics segment. Dow added, however, that price declines in most businesses have either slowed or stabilised since the first quarter of 1997.

"Dow's second-quarter earnings improvement reflects the effect of the company's strategically balanced product portfolio, the impact of above average volume growth, and continued expense control," Chief Financial Officer J. Pedro Reinhard said in a statement. "The improvement was achieved despite unfavourable currency effects and mixed prices."

Dow's Performance Plastics segment reported second-quarter operating income of $257 million, down from $325 miillion a year ago, while its Performance Chemicals unit had operating income of $233 million, down from $237 million.
Combined sales for the two Performance segments were $2.7 billion, up 3 percent.
Dow said its Chemicals and Metals segment had sales of $788 million, up from $768 million a year ago. Operating profit was $207 million, up from $205 million a year ago.
Hydrocarbons and Energy sales were up to $616 million from $595 million, while this segment posted break-even operating profit compared with a year-ago loss of $20.0 million.
